strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous benchmarking: Evaluates 15 vision models across 5 distinct pre-training paradigms (MIM, JEA, hybrid, VLM, and generative) on 7 diverse classification datasets.

Unifying perspective: Provides a clear, systematic taxonomy and mathematical formulation (Table 1) that unifies previously disparate attentive pooling and probing mechanisms (e.g., AIM, V-JEPA, CAE, SimPool, CLIP).

Principled and effective design: Efficient Probing (EP) eliminates unnecessary projection matrices while preserving expressiveness, consistently defining the Pareto frontier across accuracy, trainable parameters, and FLOPs.

Insightful diagnostic analyses: Thorough investigation into attention complementarity, attention entropy, correlation with object localization, layer-wise probing, and multi-scale Matryoshka probing provides valuable insights into representation quality beyond standard top-1 accuracy.
High clarity and presentation quality: The manuscript is well-structured, clearly written, and supported by extensive ablations and visualizations.
weaknesses: Modest algorithmic novelty: The proposed EP architecture is essentially a parameter-stripped multi-query cross-attention layer ($a_j = \text{softmax}(X^\top u_j)$ followed by a value projection). While its simplicity is well-justified and desirable for a probing protocol, the core technical novelty is incremental.

Scope limited to classification: The evaluation focuses strictly on image classification benchmarks; evaluating whether the learned attention queries translate effectively to dense visual tasks (e.g., object detection or semantic segmentation) remains unexplored.

Computational overhead during evaluation: Training the attentive probes for 90 epochs with online forward passes through the frozen backbone incurs non-trivial compute; pre-extracting and caching frozen token representations would have further highlighted the practical speedup of the probing phase.

strengths: Comprehensive benchmark: The paper conducts an extensive and rigorous comparative study of probing mechanisms across 15 foundation models spanning multiple pre-training paradigms (MIM, JEA, VLMs, generative/diffusion) and 7 classification benchmarks.

Unified framework and clean method design: The paper systematizes disparate attentive probing and pooling formulations into a coherent framework and derives Efficient Probing (EP) by eliminating redundant projection parameters while directly operating in feature space.

Compelling efficiency-accuracy trade-offs: EP demonstrates clear Pareto-dominance over existing attentive probing baselines (e.g., AIM, V-JEPA, SimPool) in terms of both parameter count and FLOPs, while closing much of the gap to full fine-tuning on models with distributed patch representations (such as MAE and SimMIM).

In-depth analysis: The paper provides insightful diagnostics, including the correlation between spatial localization / entropy and accuracy, quantitative metrics for attention map complementarity across queries, layer-wise probing robustness, and an exploration of Matryoshka representation learning.
weaknesses: Modest architectural novelty: The core architectural contribution—using a small bank of learnable query vectors without key projections for cross-attention aggregation—is a straightforward simplification of standard multi-query/cross-attention mechanisms.

Evaluation scope restricted to classification: While classification is standard for probing benchmarks, the evaluation does not extend to dense downstream tasks (e.g., semantic segmentation, object detection) where localized patch representations might exhibit even more noticeable differences.

Philosophical tension in expressive probing: As pooling mechanisms incorporate multiple queries and learnable value projections ($W_V$), the distinction between evaluating intrinsic representation quality and training a specialized adaptation head can become subtle, though the paper does well to control parameter budgets compared to prior attentive probes.

strengths: Comprehensive and systematic benchmarking across a wide spectrum of pre-training paradigms (MIM, JEA, hybrid SSL, VLMs, and generative models like DiT and AIMv2) across seven distinct datasets.
Clear and useful unifying framework (Table 1) that formalizes and compares various attentive pooling and probing mechanisms from prior literature under a consistent mathematical notation.

Efficient Probing (EP) offers an appealing accuracy-vs-parameter/FLOP Pareto trade-off, showing that standard projections (e.g., key projections) can be eliminated without degrading representational capacity.
Insightful analysis of probing behavior, including quantitative attention complementarity, correlation between attention localization/entropy and task accuracy, and layer-wise probing robustness.
weaknesses: The technical novelty of the proposed method is relatively modest, as transformation-free multi-query attention directly learns vectors in the feature space, closely resembling simplified variants of slot attention and multi-instance pooling.

The conceptual boundary between evaluation probing and lightweight parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) becomes somewhat blurred; adding learnable multi-query pooling and value projections gives the probe significant expressive capacity to adapt patch representations, deviating from traditional linear readout evaluation.

The probing protocol requires 90 full epochs with data augmentations across ImageNet-scale datasets, which incurs non-trivial computational overhead during evaluation unless frozen representations are pre-extracted.

strengths: Unifying perspective: The paper introduces a clear, principled framework that organizes existing attentive pooling/probing methods (e.g., AbMILP, AIM, SimPool, V-JEPA, CAE) and clarifies the redundant projections in standard multi-head cross-attention.

Remarkable empirical breadth: The benchmark is extraordinarily thorough, covering 15 pre-trained models across five paradigms (MIM, JEA, hybrid, VLMs, generative models) and multiple diverse datasets, demonstrating clear Pareto improvements in both parameter count and compute (FLOPs).

Insightful diagnostic analysis: The paper provides in-depth investigations into attention properties, establishing clear correlations between predictive contribution and localization/entropy, and proposing a quantifiable metric for query complementarity.

Valuable extensions: The explorations combining EP with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA), layer-wise robustness, low-shot settings, zero-shot retrieval, and Matryoshka multi-scale probing provide rich insights beyond standard probing.
Strong writing and presentation: The manuscript is well-structured, easy to follow, and supported by high-quality figures and thorough visualizations in the appendix.
weaknesses: Modest architectural novelty: The core mechanism—multi-query cross-attention with direct queries in the feature space and learnable value projections—is conceptually straightforward and represents an incremental engineering simplification over prior pooling schemes such as AIM and AbMILP.

Philosophical tension between probing and task adaptation: As the pooling module introduces multiple queries and learnable projections (e.g., up to 64 queries), the boundary between diagnostic representation evaluation (probing) and parameter-efficient task adaptation becomes blurred, which could be discussed with greater nuance.

Cached feature training not evaluated: Despite freezing the backbone, all experiments appear to backpropagate through online forward passes of the backbone rather than caching frozen patch features, which is relevant to practical efficiency in real-world probing workflows.

strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous benchmarking: The paper presents an extensive empirical evaluation covering 15 pre-trained models across five distinct paradigms (MIM, JEA, hybrid, VLM, generative) on seven diverse image classification benchmarks, establishing the most thorough study of attentive probing to date.

Clean and elegant technical formulation: The paper formalizes existing attentive pooling methods into a unified framework (Table 1) and identifies an exact redundancy in multi-head cross-attention with learnable queries, showing that the key projection can be absorbed into the query vector ($u_j = W_{Kj}^\top q_j$). This eliminates unnecessary parameters and matrix-vector operations while preserving expressivity.

Superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs: Efficient Probing (EP) consistently establishes the state-of-the-art Pareto frontier across datasets and backbones in both parameter count and computational complexity (GFLOPs), outperforming heavier architectures like V-JEPA, SigLIP, and ViT blocks.

Thorough comparative analysis with PEFT: The comparison against more than 40 LoRA configurations, BitFit, and LayerNorm tuning provides valuable context. Demonstrating that EP is complementary to LoRA and that LoRA+EP achieves superior Pareto efficiency is a compelling insight.

Insightful downstream and interpretability analyses: The study provides deep insights into query complementarity, entropy, unsupervised object localization (WSOL benchmark), zero-shot image retrieval, and rapid training convergence (achieving near-final accuracy within 10 epochs).
weaknesses: Modest methodological novelty: The core architectural contribution—collapsing the key projection and learnable query into a single query vector per predictor—is essentially a straightforward linear reparameterization. While practically effective and computationally appealing, the conceptual novelty is relatively incremental.

Conceptual tension regarding probing vs. adaptation: As attentive probing introduces learnable queries and value projection matrices across dozens of queries (up to ~1.4M–2M parameters), the boundary between pure representation probing (evaluating linear separability of pre-trained features) and lightweight downstream adaptation becomes blurred.

Minor inconsistency in the manuscript: In Section D (Limitations), the text states that exploring the synergy between probing and PEFT is left for future work, despite Section 4.2 already presenting extensive comparisons and combinations of EP with LoRA, BitFit, and LayerNorm tuning.

strengths: Comprehensive and timely empirical benchmark: The paper provides the first systematic study of attentive probing methods across a wide variety of foundation model paradigms (MIM, JEA, hybrid, VLMs, and generative/diffusion architectures) across multiple datasets.

Unifying framework and principled design: The paper cleanly formulates existing pooling and probing methods under a common mathematical framework, using this insight to derive Efficient Probing (EP) by eliminating redundant projection matrices and directly learning queries in the feature space.

Strong Pareto efficiency: EP demonstrates consistently superior accuracy-vs-parameter and accuracy-vs-compute trade-offs compared to prior attentive probing mechanisms (e.g., AIM, V-JEPA, CAE) and standard linear probing, especially on patch-distributed representations like MAE, SimMIM, and DiT.

Insightful analysis of attention properties: The analysis establishes a clear correlation between attention map quality (localization mass, entropy) and task accuracy, and demonstrates that EP queries naturally specialize into complementary object parts without requiring explicit regularization.

Thorough auxiliary investigations: The authors validate EP across low-shot regimes, layer-wise probing, unsupervised object localization, zero-shot image retrieval, and in combination with PEFT (LoRA).
weaknesses: Algorithmic novelty is relatively incremental: The core proposed mechanism—parameter-efficient multi-query cross-attention (MQCA)—primarily consists of absorbing the key projection matrix into learnable query vectors and keeping a value projection. While practically effective, it is technically straightforward.

Conceptual tension regarding probing capacity: A fundamental objective of representation probing is evaluating feature quality with minimal learnable capacity to avoid confounding backbone quality with probe expressiveness. Introducing multiple learned queries and projection matrices (yielding 1M-2M trainable parameters) borders on lightweight adaptation rather than strictly non-parametric probing.

Marginal benefits on models with strong global objectives: For models pre-trained with global representation objectives (e.g., DINOv2, DINOv3, Franca), EP yields very modest improvements over standard linear probing (+0.4% to +0.8%), limiting its practical advantage primarily to local/reconstructive pre-training paradigms.

Minor inconsistency in text: In Section D (Limitations), the paper states that evaluating the interaction with lightweight fine-tuning or adapter-based methods is left open, even though Section 4.2 and Figure 4 already provide a detailed comparison and combination with LoRA.

strengths: Comprehensive and timely benchmarking: The paper addresses a critical issue in self-supervised learning evaluation—the mismatch between masked image modeling (MIM) representations and standard linear probing—by providing the first systematic, unified study of attentive probing methods across numerous architectures (MAE, SimMIM, BEiTv2, CAPI) and datasets.

Well-motivated and efficient method: Efficient Probing (EP) elegantly strips away unnecessary projection matrices (both key and query projections) to learn queries directly in the feature space, yielding substantial reductions in parameter count and up to a 10x compute speedup compared to standard multi-head cross-attention without sacrificing classification accuracy.

Extensive empirical validation: The experimental evaluation is exceptionally thorough, covering seven classification benchmarks, backbones across various scales (ViT-S, ViT-B, ViT-L), Pareto frontier trade-off analyses (accuracy vs. parameters and FLOPs), layer-wise probing, and low-shot evaluation.

Insightful analysis and interpretability: The connection drawn between spatial localization (patch attention within ground-truth bounding boxes / entropy) and classification accuracy, along with part-specialization visualizations across heads, offers valuable qualitative and empirical insights into what attentive probes actually learn.
weaknesses: Incremental methodological novelty: Conceptually, removing linear key/query projections and performing multi-query cross-attention is a straightforward simplification of existing multi-head cross-attention / slot-attention / multiple-instance learning pooling mechanisms.

Boundary with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT): Because EP includes a trainable value projection matrix $W_V$ and multiple queries, it operates close to lightweight adapter-based PEFT. A deeper discussion or direct empirical comparison against modern lightweight PEFT methods (e.g., low-rank adaptation or bias tuning on the final block) would clarify where attentive probing ends and PEFT begins.

Minor presentation details: In Table 1, missing fine-tuning results marked with 'x' lack explicit explanation in the table caption (presumably due to lack of official fine-tuning recipes or prohibitive compute), and the transition between Equations (8) and (10) in Section 3.3 could be explained more fluidly regarding the dimensional partitioning.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: standard linear probing severely underestimates the quality of Masked Image Modeling (MIM) representations due to distributed patch tokens, while full fine-tuning is excessively expensive at scale.
Provides the first comprehensive, unified benchmark of attentive probing and pooling mechanisms across multiple SSL frameworks (MAE, SimMIM, BEiTv2, CAPI), architectures, and downstream datasets.

The proposed Efficient Probing (EP) module is conceptually simple, removing redundant key projections and learning queries directly in the feature space, which yields a strong Pareto trade-off in accuracy vs. parameters and accuracy vs. GFLOPs (up to 10x compute reduction over standard MHCA).

Thorough empirical analysis and ablation studies, including layer-wise evaluation, low-shot regimes, and an interesting analysis correlating attention entropy / localization quality to downstream classification performance.
weaknesses: The core architectural novelty is somewhat incremental, essentially amounting to removing key/query projection weights from cross-attention pooling and learning query vectors directly in the backbone token embedding space.

Attentive probing introduces additional learnable non-linear operations (cross-attention aggregation plus value projection $W_V$), which blurs the boundary between pure representation probing (evaluating linear separability) and training a small non-linear adaptation head. A deeper discussion on where this sits relative to parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) heads vs. evaluation benchmarks would strengthen the paper.
Some plots (particularly Figures 1 and 3) are quite cluttered with crowded text labels and overlapping markers, making detailed visual comparison difficult.

strengths: Relevant and timely problem: Addressing the evaluation deficit of Masked Image Modeling (MIM) under linear probing is an important topic in self-supervised visual representation learning, especially given the high computational cost of full fine-tuning at scale.

Comprehensive benchmarking and unification: The paper unifies a broad spectrum of attentive pooling and probing mechanisms (e.g., AIM, CAE, V-JEPA, SimPool, CLIP, SigLIP, CaiT) under a common mathematical formulation, providing a rigorous and much-needed empirical comparison across parameters, GFLOPs, and accuracy.

Effective and practical design: Efficient Probing (EP) simplifies cross-attention by omitting redundant key/query projections and directly optimizing learnable query vectors in the input feature space. This achieves Pareto-optimal accuracy-parameter and accuracy-compute trade-offs across multiple backbones and datasets.

Extensive experimental validation: The empirical evaluation is thorough, spanning seven classification benchmarks, multiple pre-training paradigms (MIM, JEA, VLMs), various ViT scales (ViT-S, ViT-B, ViT-L), low-shot regimes, and intermediate layer representations.

Insightful analysis and interpretability: The connection established between attention map entropy/localization quality and downstream classification accuracy, corroborated by qualitative multi-query visualizations, adds valuable analytical depth.
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: The core methodological contribution (EP) is conceptually an incremental simplification of standard cross-attention (absorbing key/query projections into learnable query embeddings with a linear value projection). While practically effective, the novelty from a modeling perspective is modest.

Narrow scope of downstream evaluation: Probing is evaluated exclusively on image classification benchmarks. Demonstrating the behavior or utility of attentive probing on dense visual tasks (e.g., semantic segmentation, object detection) would significantly strengthen the generality of the findings.

Evaluation runtime overhead: Attentive probing is trained for 90 epochs. Although the per-step parameter count and FLOPs are low, 90 epochs of training on ImageNet-1k remains a non-trivial computational cost compared to rapid linear probing or zero-shot/k-NN evaluation.

Lack of statistical variance: Across the diverse datasets—particularly fine-grained benchmarks (CUB-200, FGVC Aircraft) and low-shot subsets (5%, 10%)—results are presented as single-run point estimates without standard deviations across random seeds.
